name: Unsecured consumer loan origination at a retail bank
summary: This process takes one unsecured personal loan application from submission to funding, decline or withdrawal at a US regional retail bank. A decision engine pulls the credit report, screens identity and fraud signals and auto-approves or auto-declines most files; the rest go to underwriters, fraud analysts and, for exceptions, a senior credit officer. Approved applicants must accept the offer, often upload pay stubs and statements, and sign before loan operations books and funds the loan. Most elapsed time is spent waiting on the applicant for missing information, documents and signatures, and on work queues between underwriting, processing and funding; incomplete documents cause repeated chase loops.

baseline.org_archetype: A US regional bank with about 6,000 employees, a branch network and contact centre, and a centralised consumer lending operation using a loan origination system with a rules-based decision engine.
baseline.notes: Timing of the applicant-driven parts is anchored on the BPI Challenge 2017 event log (a Dutch bank, 2016 applications), shortened where US practice in 2019-2022 used upload portals and e-signature instead of mailed paperwork.

trigger: A consumer submits a personal loan application online, by phone or in a branch.
end_state: The loan is booked and funded, the application is declined with an adverse action notice, or it is closed as incomplete or withdrawn.

volume.seasonality: Higher in January to March (debt consolidation after the holidays and tax season) and lower in December; volumes fell in spring 2020 and recovered in 2021-2022.

evidence.note: Author estimate for a regional bank of about 6,000 employees; BPI 2017's Dutch bank handled about 2,600 applications a month (31,509 in 2016) as a scale reference.

systems.name: Loan origination system (application, workflow queues, offer and document generation)
Credit bureau interface (consumer credit report and score)
Rules-based decision engine with credit scorecard
Identity verification, fraud scoring and OFAC screening service
Secure document upload portal and imaging
Core banking loan and deposit system
Notice and letter generation with nightly print and mail batch

steps.name: Submit loan application
steps.description: The applicant starts an unsecured personal loan application on the bank's website or mobile app, or calls or visits a branch. Online applicants type identity, address, employment, income, housing cost, loan amount and purpose themselves and consent to a credit check; others are routed to a banker.

error.defect_description: Stated income, employer or housing cost typed wrongly or rounded up by the applicant.

evidence.note: Applicant effort (15 to 25 minutes) is not bank labour, so touch is 0. The 60/40 online versus assisted split is an estimate for a 2019-2022 regional bank.

steps.name: Interview applicant and key application
steps.description: A personal banker meets or phones the applicant, asks the application questions, explains products and keys the answers into the loan origination system. The banker checks a photo ID in person for branch applicants and records the ID number for the customer identification program.

error.defect_description: Keying error in income, SSN or address.

control.basis: Customer Identification Program, 31 CFR 1020.220: collect name, date of birth, address and ID number before opening the account

evidence.note: Steps of the interview from the BLS duties and CIP rule; minutes and appointment waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Run completeness, eligibility and duplicate checks
steps.description: The origination system checks that required fields are present and formatted, that the applicant meets age, residency and product limits, and that no open application exists for the same person. Applications that fail a field or eligibility rule drop into a processor's exception queue.

evidence.note: Rule-based completeness checks were standard in origination systems of the period; the 10% exception rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Contact applicant for missing information
steps.description: A loan processor opens the exception queue, reads which item is missing or inconsistent (employer, income, previous address, SSN format), and phones or emails the applicant to ask for it. The processor notes the request and the date in the file because the 30-day Regulation B clock is running.

error.defect_description: Request asks for the wrong item or omits one.

control.basis: Regulation B, 12 CFR 1002.9(c): incomplete applications must be acted on or given a notice of incompleteness within 30 days

evidence.note: Oral request for missing information is allowed by 1002.9(c); minutes and queue time are author estimates.

steps.name: Wait for applicant to supply missing information
steps.description: The application waits while the applicant finds and sends the missing details by phone, the online application or secure message. Most applicants reply within a day or two; some never reply because they have applied elsewhere.

evidence.note: BPI 2017 shows resubmission after an incomplete-file call takes a median of 23.4 hours; the share who never reply is an author estimate.

steps.name: Send written notice of incompleteness
steps.description: After several days without a reply the processor generates a written notice of incompleteness from the origination system, listing the information needed and the deadline after which the application will not be considered. The letter goes by email or post.

error.defect_description: Notice sent late or with no deadline.

control.basis: Regulation B, 12 CFR 1002.9(c)(2): written notice of incompleteness stating the information needed and a reasonable period to provide it

evidence.note: Requirement stated in 1002.9(c); timing of the processor's action is an author estimate.

steps.name: Close incomplete application at deadline
steps.description: The origination system holds the file until the deadline in the notice, typically 10 to 30 days, then closes it as incomplete and records the action for fair lending reporting. A minority of applicants respond before the deadline and the file returns to the checks.

evidence.note: Deadline length is set by bank policy within Regulation B's reasonable-time standard; BPI 2017 auto-cancels after about 26 to 30 days without response.

steps.name: Pull consumer credit report
steps.description: The origination system requests the applicant's credit report and score from a credit bureau through the bureau interface, using the consent captured in the application. Thin-file or frozen reports return without a score and are flagged for review.

control.basis: Fair Credit Reporting Act section 604: permissible purpose (consumer's application) for obtaining a consumer report

evidence.note: Bureau pull as first step of automated decisioning is described by the OCC; seconds of system time.

steps.name: Screen identity, sanctions and fraud signals
steps.description: The system matches name, date of birth, address and SSN against the credit report and an identity verification service, screens the name against the OFAC sanctions list and checks fraud alerts, address discrepancy notices and fraud scores. Any hit sends the application to the fraud queue.
outputs: identity verified or red flag alert

control.basis: Customer Identification Program (31 CFR 1020.220), OFAC sanctions regulations, and the Identity Theft Red Flags Rule under FCRA (FACT Act)

next.condition: identity mismatch, fraud alert, sanctions near-match or high fraud score

evidence.note: Checks are required by the cited rules; the 7% flag rate is an author estimate (BPI 2017 logged a formal fraud assessment on only about 1% of cases, which is treated as a lower bound).

steps.name: Score application and apply credit policy rules
steps.description: The decision engine combines the credit score with policy rules on minimum score, debt-to-income, recent delinquencies, bankruptcies and loan amount, and returns auto-approve with terms, auto-decline with reason codes, or refer to an underwriter.

error.defect_description: Rule set mis-configured for a segment; wrong terms or wrong decision.

control.basis: Board-approved credit policy and model risk management (OCC Bulletin 2011-12 principles) govern scorecard cut-offs

evidence.note: OCC describes the four automated outcomes and says most unsecured decisions are automatic; Cornerstone reports auto-decisioning approves about a third of loans. The 30/28/42 split is an author estimate within those statements.

steps.name: Investigate identity or fraud alert
steps.description: A fraud analyst opens the alert, compares the application with the credit file, prior applications and device or contact data, and calls the applicant on a number from an independent source to confirm identity or ask for a photo ID. The analyst clears the alert, declines, or closes the file when the applicant does not respond.

error.defect_description: Genuine applicant declined, or a synthetic identity cleared.

control.basis: Identity Theft Red Flags Rule: respond to detected red flags; FCRA 605A: verify identity when a fraud alert is on the file

next.condition: fraud or failed identity check: decline
applicant does not respond to verification

evidence.note: BPI 2017 reports a median 15 h 33 min and mean 3 days for the fraud assessment activity; outcome shares and hands-on minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Underwrite referred application
steps.description: A credit underwriter opens the referred file, reviews the credit report, recalculates debt-to-income from stated income and bureau debts, weighs the deposit relationship and any compensating factors, and decides to approve, counteroffer a smaller amount or higher rate, decline with reasons, or escalate a policy exception.

error.defect_description: Policy misapplied, income miscalculated or decline reason not the true reason.

control.basis: Credit policy and individual lending authority limits delegated by the board

next.condition: approval needs a policy exception above authority

evidence.note: OCC describes manual review of recommended approve or decline files; BPI 2017 shows a median 1.95 days from validation to decision. Minutes come from Cornerstone's 260 applications per underwriting FTE per month without auto-decisioning (about 30 minutes each).

steps.name: Approve policy exception
steps.description: A senior underwriter or consumer credit manager reviews the underwriter's exception memo (for example debt-to-income above policy or a low-side score override), checks the compensating factors and approves or declines in the origination system. The exception is coded for portfolio exception reporting.

control.basis: Credit policy exception approval and tracking (OCC Retail Lending booklet: policy exceptions and score overrides need defined approval authority and reporting)

evidence.note: Exception approval practice from the OCC booklet; times and approval share are author estimates.

steps.name: Second review of manual decline
steps.description: Before a manually declined application is notified, a senior underwriter re-reads the file and the stated decline reasons to confirm they are accurate, specific and consistent with policy and with similar approved files. A small share of declines are overturned into an approval or counteroffer.

control.basis: Fair lending second-review program supporting ECOA/Regulation B compliance; specific and accurate adverse action reasons (12 CFR 1002.9(b)(2))

evidence.note: Second review of declines is a common fair lending control but not required by rule; the review rate, minutes and overturn share are author estimates.

steps.name: Generate offer and pricing disclosures
steps.description: The origination system builds the offer (amount, rate, term, monthly payment) from the decision, attaches the risk-based pricing notice or credit score disclosure and posts the offer to the applicant's online account with an email alert. Offers stay open for about 30 days.

control.basis: FCRA risk-based pricing rule: notice or credit score disclosure before the consumer is contractually obligated

evidence.note: Disclosure requirement from the FTC guidance; BPI 2017 shows offers created automatically within hours of the application; 30-day validity is common practice.

steps.name: Call applicant to present offer
steps.description: A personal banker phones the applicant, confirms they received the offer, explains the rate, term and conditions such as documents still needed, and answers questions or notes a request for a different amount or term.

evidence.note: BPI 2017 logs a 'call after offers' on almost every case, with a mean activity span of about 23 minutes; hands-on minutes and the 60% call share are author estimates for a US bank.

steps.name: Applicant considers and accepts offer
steps.description: The applicant compares the offer with other lenders, sometimes asks for a revised amount, and accepts online or by phone, or lets the offer lapse. Acceptance tells the bank whether documents are still needed before closing.

next.condition: accepts; income or identity documents required

evidence.note: BPI 2017: 26.5% of cases cancelled after the offer with no reply, and about 33% cancelled overall; the 55/20 split between document and no-document approvals is an author estimate.

steps.name: Request income and identity documents
steps.description: A processor reviews the approval conditions and sends the applicant a checklist through the upload portal and email: recent pay stubs or W-2, bank statements, and a photo ID or proof of address where identity was not verified electronically.

error.defect_description: Checklist omits a condition, causing a second request later.

evidence.note: Documents typically requested are listed by Bankrate; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Wait for applicant documents
steps.description: The file waits while the applicant gathers and uploads pay stubs, statements and ID, or brings them to a branch. This is the longest wait for approved applicants.

next.condition: nothing received after a few days

evidence.note: BPI 2017 median about 7 days from offer to returned documents with mailed paperwork; the mode is shortened to 2 days for upload portals, an author adjustment.

steps.name: Chase outstanding documents
steps.description: The processor sees the file in the aged-conditions report, calls or emails the applicant to remind them what is still missing and why, and resets the follow-up date.

evidence.note: BPI 2017: 47.6% of cases had a 'call incomplete files' wait averaging 2.21 days; minutes and outcome shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Verify documents against application
steps.description: The processor opens each upload, checks pay stub dates, employer name and year-to-date income against stated income, scans bank statements for undisclosed debts or returned items, and matches the ID. Missing or stale items go back to the applicant; material differences go back to underwriting.

error.defect_description: Altered pay stub or income misread passes.

control.basis: Credit policy income verification standard (OCC Retail Lending booklet: verification practices)

evidence.note: BPI 2017: the first validation led to an incomplete-files call in about 68% of validated cases (14,935 of about 21,800) with mailed paperwork; 30% is used for upload portals. Minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Clear conditions and give final approval
steps.description: An underwriter reviews the processor's verification notes, confirms every condition is met and the final terms are within authority, and marks the loan clear to close. A loan that no longer qualifies is declined.

control.basis: Credit policy: conditions verified by a processor are signed off by a credit officer with lending authority

evidence.note: Sign-off practice follows the OCC's audit-trail expectation; minutes and decline share are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare closing package and Truth in Lending disclosure
steps.description: The processor generates the promissory note, Truth in Lending disclosure with APR and finance charge, payment schedule and any payoff instructions for debt consolidation, checks names, amounts and disbursement account, and sends the package for electronic signature.

error.defect_description: Wrong payee account, amount or name on documents.

control.basis: Truth in Lending Act, Regulation Z 12 CFR 1026.17-18: closed-end disclosures before consummation

evidence.note: Disclosure timing from Regulation Z; minutes and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Applicant signs loan agreement
steps.description: The applicant opens the electronic signature envelope, reviews and signs the note and disclosures, or signs at a branch. Some applicants take days or never sign.

evidence.note: Signing time and drop-out are author estimates for e-signature in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Pre-funding review
steps.description: A loan operations specialist checks the signed package against the approval: signatures and dates present, amount and rate match, identity and sanctions checks cleared, and the disbursement account belongs to the borrower. Defects go back to the processor.

error.defect_description: Defect missed; funded with a documentation error.

control.basis: Dual control: funding approved by operations, separate from the staff who originated and processed the loan

evidence.note: Pre-funding checks are common practice; times and the 5% defect rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Book loan and disburse funds
steps.description: The specialist books the loan in the core banking system from the origination data, sets up the payment schedule and autopay, and releases funds to the borrower's deposit account or by ACH or creditor payoff checks in the next funding run.

error.defect_description: Booking error in rate, due date or payoff amount.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: booking reconciled to the origination record

evidence.note: Bankrate says banks fund in 3 or more business days and J.D. Power (2026) that 58% of bank customers get funds within a day of approval; the next-business-day funding run is an author estimate.

steps.name: Send adverse action notice
steps.description: The system generates the decline or counteroffer notice from the reason codes, with the ECOA notice, the credit bureau's contact details, the credit score used and the right to a free report, and prints it in the nightly mail batch or sends it electronically with consent.

error.defect_description: Reasons in the notice do not match the decision.

control.basis: ECOA/Regulation B 12 CFR 1002.9(a)(2) and FCRA section 615(a): notice of adverse action with specific reasons and credit report details within 30 days

evidence.note: Content and 30-day limit stated in the cited rules; nightly batch timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Expire offer and close application
steps.description: When the applicant declines, stops responding or does not sign, the system holds the offer until its expiry date, then closes the application as withdrawn and, for counteroffers that were never accepted, sends the required adverse action notice.

control.basis: Regulation B 12 CFR 1002.9(a)(1)(iv): adverse action notice within 90 days for a counteroffer not accepted

evidence.note: BPI 2017: cancelled cases had a median duration of 31.6 days, and cancellation came on average 26.9 days after the application was completed and offers sent; the wait here is the time remaining after the earlier steps.

exceptions.name: Missing application information
exceptions.description: Required details are missing or inconsistent; the processor asks for them, and if they do not arrive the bank must send a written notice of incompleteness before closing the file.

exceptions.name: Identity or fraud alert
exceptions.description: A fraud alert, address discrepancy, identity mismatch or sanctions near-match stops the file until a fraud analyst verifies the applicant.

exceptions.name: Policy exception
exceptions.description: The underwriter wants to approve outside policy (debt-to-income or score override) and needs a senior approver.

exceptions.name: Incomplete or stale documents
exceptions.description: Uploaded pay stubs or statements are missing pages, out of date or unreadable, so the processor chases the applicant again.

exceptions.name: Income lower than stated
exceptions.description: Verified income or newly found debts change the debt-to-income ratio and the file goes back to underwriting, often for a counteroffer.

exceptions.name: Closing package defect
exceptions.description: Pre-funding review finds a missing signature, wrong amount or disbursement account mismatch and the package is reissued.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from application to final outcome, all outcomes
benchmarks.population: US bank unsecured personal loan applications, 2019-2022 (composite)

evidence.note: Composite, not a measured US median: Bankrate gives 1 to 3 business days to approve plus 3 or more to fund at banks (about 5 to 10 calendar days for funded loans); auto-declines close the same day; BPI 2017 shows withdrawn cases close after a median 31.6 days, which sets p90.

benchmarks.population: 31,409 consumer loan applications at a Dutch bank, filed in 2016 (BPI Challenge 2017 log)

evidence.note: Stated in the winning academic report; the log starts after a pre-screen, so it has no instant auto-declines and mailed offers lengthen document waits.
17,227 pending (funded), 10,430 cancelled and 3,752 denied of 31,409 cases.

benchmarks.unit: share of consumer loan applications approved
benchmarks.population: US banks and credit unions, Cornerstone Advisors 2022 benchmarks

evidence.note: 60% for institutions with auto-decisioning, 62% for those relying on underwriters.

benchmarks.population: US banks and credit unions, Cornerstone Advisors 2022 benchmarks

evidence.note: Stated in the article.
47.6% of cases passed through the wait before the first 'call incomplete files'.

pain_points.description: Approved applicants take days to return pay stubs and statements, and about a third of first uploads are incomplete, so processors run repeated chase calls while the file ages.

evidence.note: BPI 2017 shows document waits as the main bottleneck and repeated incomplete-file calls.

pain_points.description: Referred files wait one to two days in the underwriting queue, and exception files wait again for a senior approver, while faster online lenders decide the same day.

evidence.note: Bankrate contrasts bank and online lender approval times; BPI 2017 validation-to-decision median 1.95 days.

pain_points.description: A third of approved applicants never take the loan, often after shopping elsewhere during the wait, and their files sit open until the offer expires.

evidence.note: 33% of BPI 2017 applications were cancelled, mostly for no reply, after a median 31.6 days.

pain_points.description: Data typed by bankers and applicants is re-checked by hand against documents, and loan details are re-keyed or re-verified between the origination and core systems at booking.

evidence.note: Typical of origination systems of the period that were not fully integrated with the core; author judgement.

assumptions: External steps (applicant actions) carry zero touch time; the applicant's own effort is inside the waits, so the staffing comparison reflects bank labour only.
Branch, phone and online applications share one flow after keying; 40% of applications are assisted by a banker.

The decision engine split (30% auto-approve, 28% auto-decline, 42% refer) is an estimate consistent with the OCC statement that most unsecured decisions are automatic and Cornerstone's finding that auto-decisioning approves about a third of loans.

Applicant-wait times are taken from the BPI 2017 Dutch bank log and shortened for upload portals and e-signature common in US banks in 2019-2022; the Dutch log's 19.1-day median is longer than this model mainly because it has no instant auto-declines and used mailed paperwork.
The cycle-time benchmark is a composite of practitioner timelines and the BPI 2017 log rather than a measured US median; no public US event log was found.
The fraud referral rate (7%) is above the 1% formal fraud assessments in BPI 2017 because US banks route identity mismatches, fraud alerts and sanctions near-matches to a queue.
Revised offers after re-underwriting go through acceptance and document collection again; in practice some documents are reused, so this slightly overstates rework.

Stated FTEs exceed the hands-on time implied at 130 productive hours a month by about 20% to cover queue management, callbacks that reach voicemail and reporting; post-funding quality control sampling and servicing are outside this workflow.
Loaded cost = BLS May 2021 hourly wage x 1.49 (benefits: wages are 67% of compensation in financial activities, BLS ECEC Dec 2021) x 1.2 for overhead (author estimate), about 1.8 x wage.
